ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Hippocrates

code.originalText: Eight-week review: knee pain and function, the strength and balance program, sleep without diphenhydramine, the DXA result and pneumococcal vaccine

text.paragraph: Hippocrates has been to physical therapy every week and does his strength and balance exercises most days. The therapist visited his house three weeks ago; a second rail has been fitted on the stairs and night lights in the hall. He wears shoes with a back indoors. His knee pain on stairs is 3 of 10 with the gel most mornings, and he takes acetaminophen a few times a week. He had a cold two weeks ago that has cleared; he did not take the nighttime cold remedy again. He sleeps six to six and a half hours without a sleep aid. He has had no falls. He had a DXA scan this morning. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 134/72, pulse 66; weight 64.4 kg; height 168 cm, unchanged
Both knees: crepitus, no effusion; quadriceps 4+ of 5

Slower walking, knee pain on stairs and one near-fall in the past six months, found on the comprehensive geriatric assessment at intake: gait speed 0.78 m/s, Timed Up and Go 13.8 seconds, unable to hold a tandem stance for 10 seconds, grip 24 kg; cause under evaluation with a geriatric medicine consultation

S — Synthetic presenting problem of normal aging found on a comprehensive geriatric assessment; superseded at the consultation, when knee osteoarthritis with reduced leg strength and balance was diagnosed.

Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, diagnosed clinically by the ACR criteria (knee pain, age over 50, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus, bony enlargement, no warmth), with reduced quadriceps strength and balance and an increased risk of falls; KOOS JR 62
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation: a common, mild condition of aging chosen for a figure with no documented illness; not a claim about his real knees.
Potentially inappropriate over-the-counter medicines (Beers 2023): naproxen most days for about two years and diphenhydramine for sleep three or four nights a week; both stopped at intake
S — Synthetic medication history found on the deprescribing review.
Low bone mass (femoral neck T-score -1.7, total hip -1.4) with vitamin D insufficiency (24 ng/mL); FRAX 10-year risk 11 percent major and 2.6 percent hip, below treatment thresholds
S — Synthetic DXA finding at eight weeks; not a claim about his real bones.

Common cold (viral upper respiratory infection) with runny nose, sore throat and a mild cough, no fever, chest clear, oxygen saturation 97 percent; COVID-19 and influenza tests negative; resolved in about ten days
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

Guideline basis: Age-Friendly Health Systems: the 4Ms (What Matters, Medication, Mentation, Mobility) (2026); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); Updating STEADI for Primary Care: Recommendations From the American Geriatrics Society Workgroup (2025); 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); The clinician's guide to prevention and treatment of osteoporosis (2022); Osteoporosis in men: an Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline (2012); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Annual wellness visit in six weeks. Four-month review with repeat gait, balance and strength measures, vitamin D and KOOS JR. Next scheduled visit 2026-06-08: subsequent annual wellness visit. [S]
